resources.string: Lets the app automatically turn the WiFi hotspot on or off by tapping the tile in Quick Settings when the selected Bluetooth device connects/disconnects. The service only becomes active when the Bluetooth state changes.
Not enabled — tap to set up
The accessibility service was turned off — the hotspot won\'t turn on by itself in the car. Tap to turn it back on.
Warns when the watchdog service is turned off
Automatically turns the WiFi hotspot off after the watched Bluetooth device disconnects
When off, the app won\'t react to the car connecting/disconnecting. You can also toggle it from the Quick Settings tile.
Don\'t turn on when on other WiFi
When the phone is connected to WiFi with internet (e.g. at home), the hotspot won\'t turn on after the car connects.
Delay before turning off after disconnect
How many seconds to wait before turning the hotspot off after the car disconnects (0–600). Protects against brief Bluetooth dropouts (tunnel, car restart). 0 = turn off immediately.

Shows a notification when the hotspot turns on and off (also mirrors to a watch, e.g. Garmin)
Notification when the hotspot state changes (can mirror to a watch)

Tap to pick a paired device…
No paired devices found.\nPair your handsfree in Bluetooth settings first.
Interface language. \"System\" follows the device language; if that isn\'t supported, English is used.
BT Hotspot Auto service status notification

When the phone connects to the selected Bluetooth device (the car handsfree), the WiFi hotspot turns on automatically; when it disconnects, it turns off.

 The hotspot is toggled using one of three methods — tried in this order, using the first one that works on your phone:
 1. Tethering API — the silent system method (no root), requires the "Modify system settings" permission. Some manufacturers block it on their phones, though.
 2. Root shell — only on rooted phones.
 3. Accessibility service — briefly opens Quick Settings and taps the hotspot tile. Works without root even where method 1 is blocked.

 When one method fails, the app automatically uses the next one in order, so you don't have to worry about the switching.
